solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Survive like most football grounds?

definitions.meaning: to survive an attack is to hold out against it, endure it
read as two words, most grounds come '...', having a stand for spectators

explanation.surface: A quip that enduring hardship is what football grounds are built to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into WITH STAND: most football grounds have a stand, a covered block of seating for fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive a storm or assault is to endure it without giving way, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spent seven days speaking

indicators.note: speaking says the word for seven days is to be heard said out loud, not written

parts.note: a week is a period of seven days

explanation.surface: Someone tired out after a week of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent describes someone exhausted, with no strength left, so feeble in the same sense.

clue.text: Dog's tons more fun, but not male

indicators.note: but not tells us to remove the letter for male from the word before it

parts.note: merrier means jollier, more fun

explanation.surface: A claim that a dog brings much more fun, though not to a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of small, lively hunting dog, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Very black blubber

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of very dark whale fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' looks like a noun, whale fat, but here it is the verb to weep noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to cry noisily and messily, which is what a sob does.

clue.text: Gold corporation down at last for three months of the year

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word down

explanation.surface: A gold-dealing company falls in value late in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a company but is an old British joke word for a large stomach, a tum.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season, in Britain roughly September to November, a quarter of the calendar.

clue.text: Crafty recipe — one has little time

parts.note: a dish is a prepared recipe or meal
one has can be shortened to one's, giving ONES
T is the short form for time

explanation.surface: A recipe where one is short of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning and deceitful, so untrustworthy and not honest.

clue.text: Father takes daughter home

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad brings his daughter back to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is informal slang for someone's flat or house, where they live.

clue.text: Rice recipe: unlimited Apulian cooking

indicators.note: cooking says the remaining letters are worked up into a new arrangement
unlimited says the word Apulian loses its limits, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rice dish from Apulia, the heel of Italy, being made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' removes the A and N from APULIAN, leaving PULIA; 'cooking' rearranges those five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a spiced rice dish cooked in stock, of Middle Eastern and South Asian origin.

clue.text: Waste material one's thrown in underground cell

parts.note: dung is animal excrement, waste matter

indicators.note: thrown suggests the word one is tossed about into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone flung into a cell full of muck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark prison cell, traditionally beneath a castle.

clue.text: A Balkan national hugs British gymnast

indicators.note: hugs means one word wraps its arms around the letter for British

parts.note: a Croat is a person from Croatia, a Balkan country

explanation.surface: A Balkan athlete embraces a British competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs feats of balance and agility, much like a gymnast.

clue.text: Little Sarah working in hairdressers

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sarah
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Young Sarah has a job at a hairdresser's.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a business premises for hairdressing or beauty treatment.

clue.text: Dance club certain about politician and old disturbance

indicators.note: about here tells us the word for certain goes around to the far side of the rest, after them

parts.note: a disco is a club for dancing
MP is a Member of Parliament
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A nightclub is sure there will be trouble over a politician and an old figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Discomposure is a state of agitation or ruffled calm, a disturbance of composure.

clue.text: Company conflict over gamble shows lack of courage

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the earlier pieces above the next one

parts.note: war is armed conflict
to dice is to gamble, play at dice

explanation.surface: A firm's dispute about a bet reveals its nerve has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is timidity in the face of danger, the absence of bravery.

clue.text: Cut up about wife being clever

indicators.note: about means one word is placed around the letter for wife

parts.note: to shred is to cut up into strips

explanation.surface: Someone upset about his wife being so bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like upset but means to shred.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute, sharp in judgement, so clever in a practical way.

clue.text: To incite's about right: rider's put his foot in it?

definitions.text: rider's put his foot in it?
definitions.note: a horse rider puts a foot in this loop hung from the saddle; the phrase usually means making a gaffe

indicators.note: about means the phrase is split open around the letter for right

parts.note: to stir up is to incite, provoke

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble around a rider who has made a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the metal loop hanging from a saddle that supports the rider's foot.

clue.text: The French boy's time at school

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A French lad's period in the classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, a timetabled slot during the school day.

clue.text: Heartfelt selection of words in ceremony

indicators.note: selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A choice of moving words for a formal occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt means genuinely felt, honest and unfeigned.

clue.text: Depression in gloomy place, on ecstasy

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the earlier pieces above the next

parts.note: dim means dark, gloomy
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone depressed in a dark spot, high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood but is a small hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimple is a small hollow in the skin, a slight dip in a surface.

clue.text: Occasional short insect breaks inside camping shelter

indicators.note: breaks says one piece breaks into the phrase that follows, splitting it

parts.note: in means inside
a tent is a shelter for camping

indicators.note: short says the word for the insect loses its final letter

parts.note: a termite is an ant-like insect

explanation.surface: A bug sometimes gets into a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like a placement signal but simply supplies its synonym; the real container is the phrase 'inside camping shelter', which 'breaks' opens for the 'short' insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermittent means stopping and starting at intervals, happening now and then.

clue.text: Firm losing small data chart

indicators.note: losing tells us the word for firm drops the letter for small

parts.note: stable means firm, steady

explanation.surface: A company shrinking, shown on a graph of figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective, steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A table sets out figures in rows and columns, a grid of data.

clue.text: Church melody form — Christian, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A musical form found in Christian worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a song of praise sung in church services, a Christian sacred song.

clue.text: Scholar to talk endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for talk loses its final letter

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering, talking on and on

explanation.surface: A learned person who talks without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English to 'rabbit on' is to talk at length about little.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher, learned in the law, a scholar.

clue.text: Mad about Queen and Wedgwood, perhaps

indicators.note: about means the word for mad goes around the letters for Queen

parts.note: potty is informal British for mad, crazy
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone crazy about the monarch and fine china.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood is an English maker of fine ceramics, so an example of glazed earthenware ware.

clue.text: Label's strange with odd letters missing

indicators.note: dropping the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of strange leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: A label that looks odd because letters have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag is a small attached label giving a name or price.

clue.text: Greek character wanting English dish

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person wants an English meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked meal of filling in pastry, a kind of food served in a dish.

clue.text: Always envious, for constantly popular person

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
green means envious, as in green with envy

explanation.surface: Forever jealous of someone who never goes out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen is a performer or song with lasting appeal, never losing favour.
